sections.text:
Our opponents cannot even take refuge in the excuse of ignorance, since they handle the argument with such deliberate craft. They are plainly angry with us because we complete the doxology to the Only-begotten together with the Father and do not separate the Holy Spirit from the Son. Hence they call us innovators, revolutionaries, inventors of expressions, and every other reproach they can devise. I am so far from being distressed by their insults that, were it not for the grief and continual pain caused by their loss, I could almost thank them for their blasphemy as providing an occasion for blessing, for the Lord says, “Blessed are you when they revile you for my sake.”

Their complaint is this: the Son, they say, is not with the Father but after the Father. Therefore glory should be offered to the Father through the Son, not with the Son; for “with him” signifies equality of honor, whereas “through him” indicates subordinate service. Likewise, they say, the Spirit must not be ranked with the Father and the Son but beneath the Son and the Father—not coordinated but subordinated, not counted together but counted underneath. With such technical manipulation of words they distort the simplicity and uncontrived character of the faith. How then can they claim pardon on account of ignorance when their own meddlesome subtlety does not allow others to remain ignorant of the scheme?

Let us first ask them what they mean when they say that the Son is “after the Father.” Is he later in time, lower in order, or inferior in dignity? As to time, no one should be so senseless as to say that the Maker of the ages holds a second place in time, since no interval stands between the natural relation of the Son to the Father.

Even according to ordinary human thought, it is impossible to conceive the Son as younger than the Father. Father and Son are thought together by their relation. Moreover, things are called later in time when they are nearer to the present and earlier when farther from it. The events of Noah are earlier than those of Sodom because they are farther removed from our present, while the events of Sodom are later because they lie nearer. But to measure the life that transcends every time and every age by distance from the present is not merely irreverent; it is the height of folly.

The Father's priority cannot be imagined as a stretch of time preceding the Son. No thought or conception can rise above the Lord's generation. John has enclosed our understanding within two expressions: “In the beginning was the Word.” Thought cannot get outside “was,” and imagination cannot pass beyond “beginning.” However far backward the mind runs, it never escapes the “was”; however much it strains to see beyond the Son, it cannot climb above “the beginning.” Therefore true religion teaches us to conceive the Son together with the Father.

If they imagine the Son to be beneath the Father as though in a lower place—the Father seated above and the Son pushed to a lower seat—let them say so plainly, and the obvious absurdity of the view will refute itself. Those who deny that the Father pervades all things do not even preserve the consistency of their own reasoning, for sound faith believes that God fills all things. Nor do those who distribute “above” and “below” between Father and Son remember the prophet: “If I ascend into heaven, you are there; if I descend into Hades, you are present.”

To assign spatial position to incorporeal realities is already ignorant. But their position also clashes openly with Scripture: “Sit at my right hand,” and, “He sat down at the right hand of the Majesty of God.” The “right hand” does not designate a lower region. It expresses equality of relation and the magnificence of the Son's honor. Scripture does not speak bodily, as though there were a literal right and left in God; it uses the language of the place of honor to manifest the dignity of the Son.

If they therefore retreat to saying that “after” means inferior in dignity, let them learn that Christ is “the Power of God and the Wisdom of God,” “the image of the invisible God,” “the radiance of his glory,” and the One whom the Father has sealed. Are such texts humiliations, or do they proclaim the majesty of the Only-begotten and the equality of his glory with the Father?

Hear also the Lord himself: “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father”; “when the Son comes in the glory of his Father”; “that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father”; “we beheld his glory, glory as of the Only-begotten from the Father”; and “the only-begotten God, who is in the bosom of the Father.” The Father's bosom is a fitting seat for the Son; the place of a footstool belongs to enemies forced into submission.

The language of standing and sitting signifies, as I understand it, the fixed and wholly stable character of the divine nature, while the right hand signifies equality of honor. It is therefore rash to deprive the Son of participation in the doxology and treat him as though he deserved a lower rank.

translator_notes: Direct Mercy translation from Basil's Greek PG 32 text.
Sections 13–15 preserve Basil's distinction between temporal sequence, spatial imagery, and equality of divine honor.
Biblical citations are translated from Basil's Greek wording.
